'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Battle of Bakhmut]]
****[[Russia]] claims that it captured the village of Klishchiivka in [[Donetsk Oblast]], south of [[Bakhmut]], and the village of Lobkove in [[Zaporizhzhia Oblast]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/1/20/russia-claims-capture-of-village-near-ukraines-bakhmut (Al Jazeera)]

**A bomb blast [[derailment|derails]] a [[passenger train]] in Peshi village, [[Kachhi District]], [[Balochistan, Pakistan|Balochistan]], [[Pakistan]], injuring 13 people. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/1/20/blast-derails-passenger-train-in-pakistans-balochistan-report (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Jihadist insurgency in Burkina Faso]]
**The [[Burkina Faso Armed Forces]] rescue 62 women and four babies [[kidnap]]ped by [[Jihadism|jihadists]] in [[Arbinda]], [[Sahel Region]], on January 15. [https://www.voanews.com/a/army-frees-abducted-women-babies-in-burkina-faso/6927629.html (AFP via Voice of America)]
*The [[United States Department of the Treasury]] designates the [[Russia]]n [[paramilitary]] organization [[Wagner Group]] as a [[Transnational organized crime|transnational criminal organization]], allowing provisions for [[international sanctions]]. [https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2023/01/20/washington-designates-russia-s-wagner-criminal-organization_6012393_4.html (AFP via ''Le Monde'')]

**The [[Bank of Japan]] reports that [[inflation]] in [[Japan]] increased by 4.0% in December, the highest recorded increase [[Economic history of Japan|since 1981]]. '''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2023 Nyingchi avalanche]]
**Twenty-eight people are killed and 53 others are rescued during an [[avalanche]] at a [[tunnel]] in [[Nyingchi]], [[Tibet]], [[China]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/1/20/death-toll-in-tibet-avalanche-rises-to-20-eight-still-missing (Al Jazeera)]
*A [[Dominica|Dominican]] man who was lost in the [[Caribbean Sea]] for 24 days is rescued by the [[Colombian Navy]]. [https://apnews.com/article/politics-caribbean-colombia-dominica-c2c569a33d23e8be8414ada6d864d8f4 (AP)]
*Seven people are killed and over 50 are injured in a collision between a bus carrying students and a van in [[Radella]], near [[Nuwara Eliya]], [[Sri Lanka]]. [https://www.gulftoday.ae/news/2023/01/21/seven-killed-over-50-injured-as-van-school-bus-collide-in-sri-lanka (Gulf Today)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
***[[Prime Minister of South Korea|Prime Minister]] [[Han Duck-soo]] announces the termination of [[South Korea|the country]]'s [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|indoor mask mandate]], with the exception of [[Public transportation in South Korea|public transport]] and [[Healthcare in South Korea|medical facilities]], effective January 30. [https://news.abs-cbn.com/overseas/01/20/23/south-korea-to-drop-most-indoor-mask-restrictions (AFP via ABS-CBN News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Sagarejo shooting]]
**A man [[mass shooting|opens fire]] from a balcony in [[Sagarejo]], [[Kakheti]], [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]], killing five people and injuring five others. The gunman later commits [[suicide]]. [https://globalnews.ca/news/9423729/georgia-sagarejo-shooting-police/ (Global News)]
*[[Rishi Sunak seatbelt incident]]
**[[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|UK Prime Minister]] [[Rishi Sunak]] is [[Fine (penalty)|fined]] [[pound sterling|£]]100 by [[Lancashire Constabulary]] for failing to wear a [[seat belt]] while recording a video for [[social media]] in the back of a moving car. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-64353054 (BBC News)]
